144.solution: \(eV_0 = h\nu - \phi_0\), so the line cuts the \(V_0\) axis at \(-\dfrac{\phi_0}{e}\). Hence \(\phi_0 = e \times OB\) in joules; \(OA\) is the threshold frequency and the slope is \(\dfrac{h}{e}\).

145.solution: \(r_n = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 n^2h^2}{\pi me^2}\), so \(r_2 = \dfrac{4\varepsilon_0h^2}{\pi me^2}\) and \(I = mr_2^2 = \dfrac{16\varepsilon_0^2h^4}{\pi^2me^4}\).

146.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
146.subtopic: de Broglie Wavelength and Matter Waves
146.solution: The orbit holds a whole number of waves: \(n\lambda = 2\pi r\), so \(\lambda = \dfrac{2\pi r}{n}\).

150.subtopic: Band Theory, Doping, and Semiconductor Types
150.solution: In (1) \(E_F\) is midway between the bands (intrinsic), in (2) it is near the valence band (p-type) and in (3) near the conduction band (n-type). So (2), (1), (3) are p, intrinsic and n.
